Core: Threadbare · Session 8

How do you make a big challenge feel doable?

Use your GDD to build a first backlog on your Project Board. Then choose an important task or question and start working on it in Godot.

60 minutes Problem decomp Godot
Play Create Share Reflect
Play

What area of game making calls you?

5 min

Game making is a multidisciplinary endeavor - there are many fields of work and many tasks up for grabs. So think about a video game you like:

  • What's one thing you would have liked to create in it?
  • If it was something like sound, do you see yourself making sound effects (SFX) for your StoryQuest?

Keep those interests in mind as you look at the work your StoryQuest needs. Your board can help your team see the different jobs ahead and decide who wants to take them on.

Create

Build your first backlog and break down tasks

20 min

Start with the GDD your team drafted last session. Open your shared Project Board and use the GDD to add your first batch of tasks and questions.

What work can your team already see? Add a first batch of issues to your backlog. Some will be clear tasks. Others may be questions you need to investigate, such as whether you can remix an existing enemy or how a new behavior might work.

Some issues will feel big, daunting, or full of unknowns. When one does, break it into smaller, more manageable tasks on the board, so your backlog fills up with pieces you can actually pick up and start instead of one overwhelming, multi-part job.

You do not need to identify every task today. Your board is a starting plan. Add and change issues as you learn more while building.

Create

Choose where to start

5 min

Look over your backlog together. Is there something important that your team is unsure how to make, especially something other work may depend on? That could be a good place to start. Choose one manageable task or investigation and move it into Todo.

Starting with an unknown can help you learn early whether a key part of your StoryQuest is possible. If your team needs a simpler first task to get moving, choose that instead.

Create

Get to work

25 min

Work on the task or investigation your team chose. Try an approach in Godot, test what happens, and talk about what you learn. You might complete a small task today, or you might discover that the issue needs to change or be divided further.

Use the scene setup guide below if your task involves building a new scene. For other tasks, find the relevant help in the Guide Hub.

…and in the Project Board

5 min

Your task

When your team's Project Board is ready, submit a link to it on the Platform. In your submission, briefly say what your team chose to tackle first and what you learned from trying it.

This is your first board submission, so instructors can see your plan and follow your progress. Keep adding, moving, and revising issues as you build. Mark an issue completed only when that work is finished.

Reflect

Before you move on

Reflect

Your team used its GDD to start a backlog, chose a place to begin, and learned something by trying it. Keep using the board to make the next steps visible, including questions that still need answers.
